title: Women's school in Afghanistan and school supplies sent with Rod Alexander
summary: Addie visits a girls' school in Kabul and arranges supplies to be carried by Rod Alexander's dance troupe.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Another after effect of this tour is when we were in Afghanistan I visited what's called the Women's Welfare Institute there, you know education facilities are quite primitive and practically non-existent the women over here. And this is a school that runs from kindergarten to the equivalent of high school. So when I went to visit the school the director thought I was from UNESCO for the first. She started telling me all the things that I needed about. And so it's obvious they really need equipment for their little school you know because they have a hard time the women you know are segregated and much oppressed and kept in complete segregation. They wear robes
and you know they're little people
That's nice you wouldn't have food with your head

but but ANTA just sent Rod Alexander over with the dance troupe and they were going to play Kabul and I had been trying to figure out how to send some stuff to the school over there because the packages I wanted to send were too big for the diplomatic pouch you know and and it's pretty hard to get things through the border actually there through Pakistan and Afghanistan so we promoted a set of world books from the Growlier Society and then we bought a bunch of stuff and I bought patterns and slates and chalk and paint and crayons and pencil paper things that we just take pretty much for granted you know in this country anyway I had three big cartons of school supplies going over with Rod Alexander them to be presented the school
